title: Signed shifts and finite-word transport for normalized pullback comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes $W$ below are noetherian and finite dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, with the meaning and the common full integral constructible categories of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $R_{E,W}=\lim_{n\geq1}(A_{E,n})_W$ on the small pro-etale site, and use framework and PBC completed pullbacks $F^s_{h,E},F^p_{h,E}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $I_{W,E}$ for restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient identity, giving the integral identity equivalence. All equalities below use these fixed identity transports; we suppress $I$ when source and target already have the same module presentation. For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$, let $G_{h,E}$ be ordinary derived module pullback on the completed rings. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $R_{E,T}$ set
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T),\qquad H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1],$$
with the actual quotient transitions and $s_Q((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].
For each such tower, use the normalized derived comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison],
$$\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q,$$
where $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms and $\iota_I:\lim I_\bullet\to H(I_\bullet)$ has coordinates $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Write $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}:IF^s_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,E}I$ for this comparison with the defining realization identifications, and $b^{\rm int}_{h,E}$ for its restriction to the full integral constructible categories.
For every $r\in\mathbf Z$ the natural signed cone isomorphism $H(Q[r])\to H(Q)[r]$ is $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r y,x)$ in reversed cone coordinates. It descends through the specified representative comparison to the framework pullback shifts with exactly the predicates $\operatorname{ShiftCoordinates}$ and $\operatorname{ShiftDescent}$ of [def-fd-integral-pullback-shift-coordinates]. With the canonical exact-functor shifts on the PBC realization and coefficient transport,
$$\operatorname{shift}^p_{r,K}\circ b^{\rm amb}_{h,E,K[r]}=b^{\rm amb}_{h,E,K}[r]\circ\operatorname{shift}^s_{r,K}.$$
It fixes every normalized augmentation $(0,z)$; the same shift square holds for the scalar comparison induced by any degree-zero strict map $d_\bullet$ on both cone coordinates.
Suppose the primitive unit, composition and scalar maps are the actual maps identified in [lem-fd-pbc-completed-compositor-normalization, lem-fd-scalar-pullback-realization-identification], and the realization models retain the entire-system counits as in [lem-fd-pullback-augmentation-counit-matching]. For each finite composable word $w$ of scheme-isomorphism pullbacks and finite coefficient extensions, let $r_{w,C}:\widehat w\mathcal LC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LwC$ be its counit-built comparison [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution]; restrict to normalized systems with constructible-complete intermediate realizations. Every specified system comparison $t:w\Rightarrow w'$ is realized by
$$\widehat t_{\mathcal LC}=r_{w',C}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(t_C)\circ r_{w,C}.$$
This identification intertwines the two presentations by the above $b$, respects the signed shifts, and carries the entire-diagram equalities of [lem-trf-quotient-system-mixed-coherence] to the corresponding identities for the actual integral operations: associativity and units for arbitrary finite scheme compositions, equality of scheme maps, repeated fields, and successive scalar extensions. The scalar associator is the ordinary tensor associator conjugated by the specified $\chi$ maps; equal fields use multiplication followed by completeness. The same identities hold after raw rationalization and for inverse comparisons. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on quotient complexes is imposed.

proof.text: Work in the common completed-ring module presentation fixed in the statement. The pro-etale exact-product lemma applies to the sheaf of rings $R_{E,U}$, so the termwise countable products used by the Roos functor represent the required derived products. For each $r$, finite pullback, reduction and restriction of scalars commute with degree reindexing and multiply the differential by $(-1)^r$. Their canonical comparisons therefore identify $Q_{h,E}(P[r])_n$ with $Q_{h,E}(P)_n[r]$. They also identify each transition: in degree $i$ both transition maps are the original quotient map on $P^{i+r}$. Taking products gives precisely the productShift in the coordinate definition, and conjugates $1-s_{Q(P[r])}$ to $(1-s_{Q(P)})[r]$. No quotient tensor map is being declared flat.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product model; agent-written specialization to the specified finite pullback towers

proof.text: Apply the signed strict-Roos shift lemma to this tower. In its reversed coordinates put $M=\prod_nQ_n$ and $a=1-s_Q$. The source differential on $H(Q[r])$ is $(y,x)\mapsto(-(-1)^rdy-ax,(-1)^rdx)$, while that on $H(Q)[r]$ is $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r(-dy-ax),(-1)^rdx)$. Thus $c_r(y,x)=((-1)^ry,x)$ is a chain map; it is its own inverse after reindexing. This is the exact pair of component equations of ShiftCoordinates, not an unsigned cone identification. The cited lemma gives naturality and $c_0=1$, $c_r[s]c_s=c_{r+s}$; the sign identity is $(-1)^{r+s}=(-1)^r(-1)^s$. Also $c_r(0,z)=(0,z)$, with the degree of $z$ reindexed.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone; explicit signed cochain calculation and the existing strict-Roos shift/localization lemma

proof.text:
The sign also commutes with the normalized comparison to $R\lim$. Choose $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ as in the strict-Roos comparison. Its shift is again an eligible resolution: injectivity of terms is unchanged by reindexing, and K-injectivity follows by shifting an acyclic source back, applying its defining null-homotopy property, then shifting the homotopy. The inclusion $j_I(z)=(0,z)$ obeys $c_{I,r}j_{I[r]}=j_I[r]\lambda_{I,r}$, where $\lambda$ is the termwise limit shift. Naturality gives $H(q)[r]c_{Q,r}=c_{I,r}H(q[r])$. Substitution into $\rho_Q=[j_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$ gives
$$\rho_Q[r]\,[c_{Q,r}]=\operatorname{shift}^{R\lim}_{r,Q}\,\rho_{Q[r]}.$$
Here the right-hand shift is the canonical shift computed by $\lambda_{I,r}$ on the shifted K-injective resolution. The resolution independence in the cited comparison makes this identity independent of $q$. It also proves compatibility with every normalized augmentation, since its shifted product coordinate is zero.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, K-injective model and ordinary-limit inclusion; signed refinement written by the worker

proof.text:
Descend the coordinate isomorphism through the retained representative comparison. A flat-term K-flat $P$ remains good after any integer shift: its terms are reindexed flat terms, and $A\otimes P[r]\cong(A\otimes P)[r]$ for any acyclic $A$, by the total-tensor sign convention, so this tensor is acyclic. The well-definedness theorem gives the descended pullback functor and its natural comparisons on good representatives, independent of resolutions. Conjugating the localized $c_r$ by those comparisons defines its shift $d_r$. Solving for $d_r$ gives, with localization comparisons $\eta$ inserted,
$$\varepsilon_P[r]d_{r,QP}=\eta_{F_g(P)}Q(c_{r,P})\varepsilon_{P[r]}D_g(\eta_P^{-1}),$$
which is exactly ShiftDescent. Naturality of $c_r$ makes this formula commute with every resolving comparison and its inverse; the localization universal property transports the identity, composition and shift coherence equations. Hence it gives a coherent structure on the descended functor, not a choice made independently for each object. On the PBC side, the finite-pullback strict-tower comparison identifies $Lh^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(K_\bullet)$ with the same strict tower $Q_{h,E}(P)$ by exactly the finite evaluation comparisons fixed in the PBC definition, and states $s^B_{K,r}\circ b_{h,K[r]}=b_{h,K}[r]\circ s^V_{K,r}$, where $s^V$ is the canonical reduction/tower-pullback shift and $s^B$ is the termwise levelShift of step 1. Applying $R\lim$ with its canonical shift, and noting that the restriction $I$ along the identity coefficient isomorphism is termwise and commutes strictly with reindexing, the canonical exact-functor shift of $F^p_{h,E}$ is $R\lim$-shift after $R\lim(\operatorname{levelShift})$. Combining this with step 3 and the formula above proves the displayed ambient shift square. Restriction to the full integral categories is valid because the characterization theorem explicitly closes them under shifts.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; agent-written descent through the specified natural representative comparisons

proof.text:
For a degree-zero strict tower map $d_\bullet$, write $D=\prod_nd_n$ after the specified tensor/product comparisons. The cone map is $(y,x)\mapsto(Dy,Dx)$, so
$$c_r(Dy,Dx)=((-1)^rDy,Dx)=(D((-1)^ry),Dx).$$
This proves the scalar shift square before localization, including its zero-coordinate augmentation. The scalar realization-identification lemma identifies this very diagonal cone map, after conjugating by $\chi$, with the actual scalar/pullback comparison in the PBC presentation. The normalized scalar-completion comparison states that $\chi$ and its inverse commute with the specified shifts. Thus conjugating the preceding equality proves the scalar square with the actual scalar maps, and step 3 applies on its derived-limit side. This argument only uses degree zero and strict compatibility of $d_\bullet$; it never inverts an individual $d_n$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, functorial cone map; agent-written degree-zero diagonal calculation

proof.text:
Use the simultaneous realization system supplied by augmentation/counit matching. The compositor-normalization lemma identifies its scheme units and compositors with the actual PBC maps, and the scalar-identification lemma identifies its mixed scalar map with the actual one. In particular this is the system retaining the whole-system counit at every intermediate realization. Apply counit-realization substitution to it, on exactly the normalized systems with constructible-complete intermediate realizations stipulated here. It gives $r_{O,C}=\mathcal L(O(e_C))b_{O,\mathcal LC}$ for a primitive operation, and recursively $r_{vw,C}=r_{v,wC}\widehat v(r_{w,C})$. Starting from the empty word with identity comparison gives all finite words. For a primitive comparison the cited theorem gives
$$\widehat t_{\mathcal LC}=r_{w',C}^{-1}\mathcal L(t_C)r_{w,C}.$$
For composable $t:w\to w'$ and $u:w'\to w''$, the two adjacent $r_{w',C}$ factors cancel, giving the same formula for $ut$; the cited substitution theorem also gives it after whiskering. Induction on the construction of a specified comparison proves the formula for every such comparison. Applying the same recursion to the primitive intertwinings by $b$ proves that these identifications intertwine the two presentations for every word.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, counit normalization; agent-written application of the cited whole-system substitution theorem

proof.text:
Apply the entire-system coherence equations of the mixed-coherence lemma. For any two equal comparison paths $t,u:w\Rightarrow w'$, functoriality gives $\mathcal L(t_C)=\mathcal L(u_C)$; conjugating by the same $r_{w',C}^{-1}$ and $r_{w,C}$ proves equality of their actual integral realizations. Step 6 identifies these realizations with the primitive actual maps and their whiskered composites. This proves the mixed composition equation, arbitrary finite associativity and scheme units, equality for equal scheme maps, and the scalar unit and tower equations, including repeated fields. No faithfulness of separate finite evaluations is used. More explicitly, the scalar associator is, by counit substitution,
$$\chi_{M/E,K}\alpha^\otimes_K(\chi_{L/E,K}^{-1}\otimes^L1)\chi_{M/L,\widehat S_{L/E}K}^{-1}.$$
For $E=L$, the same theorem identifies the system multiplication unit with multiplication followed by completeness. Thus these are the claimed specified scalar maps, rather than unnamed associators having only the same source and target.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, realization functor; agent-written conjugation of existing entire-system coherence equations

proof.text: The word identifications also respect the signed shifts. On the Roos side, every strict degree-zero operation map commutes with $c_r$ by the diagonal calculation of step 5; the quotient augmentations commute because $c_r(0,z)=(0,z)$. For the counit in the simultaneous models, augmentation/counit matching identifies it with $[q]^{-1}[\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet]$. Shifting $q$ and the ordinary limit projections commutes with this entire-tower map, as in step 3. Its change-of-rings adjunct uses degree-zero tensor maps, so has the same compatibility. Thus every factor $b_{O,\mathcal LC}$ and $\mathcal L(O(e_C))$ in $r_{O,C}$ commutes with the specified shifts; for scalar factors use also the shift compatibility of $\chi$. The recursive formula for $r_{vw,C}$ now proves its shift square by induction on word length. Inserting those squares on the two sides of the formula for $\widehat t$ proves the asserted signed compatibility for each comparison and hence for every transported equality.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, whole-system counit computed on K-injectives; agent-written induction through the retained word comparisons

proof.text:
Finally raw rationalization sends an integral map $f$ to $f\otimes1$. By its definition, composition is bilinear and the induced shifts act on this same scalar-localized Hom, so applying it to either side of every equality above preserves that equality and all comparison isomorphisms. For the inverse of any comparison $t$, the transported formula is
$$(r_{w',C}^{-1}\mathcal L(t_C)r_{w,C})^{-1}=r_{w,C}^{-1}\mathcal L(t_C^{-1})r_{w',C}.$$
Likewise multiplying a shift square on the appropriate sides by the inverse comparison gives its inverse shift square. These operations preserve the already proved normalized unit and word identities. Throughout, towers and their counits were entire derived diagrams; only good ambient representatives were used. The mixed-coherence and substitution statements explicitly require neither finite Tor-amplitude of quotient complexes nor flat finite coefficient maps, so no such extra hypothesis has entered.
